meta.title: 29 Things I Wish I Knew Before Visiting Vietnam

My Health Insurance (Safetywing): https://safetywing.com/nomad-insurance/?referenceID=25111590&campaign=vietnam&utm_campaign=vietnam&utm_source=25111590&utm_medium=Ambassador

I'm only halfway through this presentation but 3 things come to mind having been to Vietnam 4 times.
 The insurance is not very good when you're over 70.
 Time your trip with Tet celebrations in mind. Hotels are over booked And many restaurants are closed.
Most importantly when you rent a motorbike confirm which handle controls the front brake or the back break because it depends on where they work manufactured for left hand driving or right hand driving and you don't want to squeeze your front brake and go head over heels as I have done.

Nice video. My wife is American Lao. We usually go to Thailand and Laos for vacation. We went to Vietnam a few weeks ago. We did not like it at all. The food was not that good. The traffic is so bad. They do not move or stop for you. In Thailand and Laos they will. The streets and roads are in bad shape. Trash is everywhere. We went to Hoi An. It smelled and it the worst for trash. We left before nightfall. The hotels we stayed at. Loud music late into the night near by. The people were cold. We have family married into Vietnamese. They are warm friendly and kind. We will not be going back again. The worst was the night markets. High pressure to buy something every few feet. Again. Thailand and Laos don’t do that. AC in buildings in public have minimal AC. You move and you will sweat. Only hotels and certain places have cold AC.
Other markets have no fans and are in the open.

comments.author: @Specialone888-c5v
comments.text: Don’t believe all of these fake social media influencers and lying YouTube posts who make Vietnam look like the hot new paradise on earth because it isn’t.  Just went to visit Vietnam and check it out and it’s a 6 out of 10.  Thailand is much better 9/10 for many reasons like much better infrastructure, the politeness of the local Thai people.  In Vietnam the vibe is more aggressive & rude like back in America and the language barrier is worse than you think so you can’t communicate with the people.  Plus the big elephant sitting in the living room is the stigma of the horrible Vietnam war dead ghosts still hangs where 58,000 Americans died and 3 million Vietnamese died gives it a weird paranormal feeling.  Reminded me of the killing fields of Cambodia with pol pot who killed 3 million of his own people or visiting world war 2 battlefields in Europe where millions were murdered with the same weird ghost paranormal feelings.  In Vietnam it was a constant surreal experience & feeling to think that my uncle fought only 49 miles from our beach front resort in Da Nang in one of the bloodiest battles of the Vietnam war where thousand perished in bloody door to door combat.  I couldn’t stop thinking about it and remembering his stories of almost being killed by a booby trap bomb toy bear he picked up and exploded in his face placed by the enemy.
